AUSENTE: numeric values and widths for quota plus batch plus inode number limits
AUSENTE: full layout and initialization of superblock info plus inode extensions plus virtual area descriptors
AUSENTE: semantics of memory policy plus seal handling plus freeze control plus page cache insertion helpers
AUSENTE: preservation transport guarantees including physical address stability across live update

findings.text: Two build variants provide a global release routine for virtual mappings. The minimal build forwards directly to generic heap release. The full build defers when in interrupt context, tolerates a null address, warns on unknown areas, optionally restores direct map permissions, releases backing pages, then frees the page array and descriptor.

A global atomic release path usable from interrupt context records the address on a per processor deferred list with lockless insertion and schedules associated work when the list changes from empty. It tolerates a null address and forbids use from non maskable interrupt context.

The memory file creation system call sanitizes supplied flags, allocates a kernel copy of the user name, derives descriptor close on exec behavior from creation flags, creates the backing file and installs it as a new descriptor.
Module initialization registers a live update file handler for memory files and treats unsupported operation as benign while propagating other registration failures with a diagnostic.

Superblock accounting state including free space, inode sequence, full number mode and policy pointer is guarded by a raw spin lock held in superblock info. Reserve and free paths hold it around quota checks and updates, while policy fetch holds it across pointer copy and reference acquisition to prevent replace versus use races.

Regular mounts enforce inode space quota and allocate sequential numbers skipping the zero value, with wrap handling that restarts the sequence and warns on wide builds when full width numbers are disabled and the sequence passes the unsigned maximum. Kernel internal mounts use a per processor batched allocator touching the shared lock only at batch boundaries and ignoring width compatibility concerns. Freeing returns a fixed per inode quantum plus caller supplied space under lock when quota is enabled.

Two configuration variants exist for superblock policy retrieval. One returns no policy unconditionally. The other returns a referenced copy of the configured policy under lock when present and no policy otherwise.

Flag updates first delegate case folding validation then translate persistence flags for no access time plus append only plus immutable into inode state while leaving no dump without inode effect, applying changes under a mask that includes case folding. Enabling folding requires encoding support on directory inodes with optional emptiness check, while both enable and disable paths reject non empty directories when a dentry is supplied. Alternate builds reject folding entirely or ignore all flag updates.
Shmem inode state embeds a directory offset tracking context retrievable from the generic inode through a container conversion.

One configuration delegates inode creation to a shared helper, while a constrained variant creates memory filesystem inodes through the ram library and reports no space failure when creation fails. Size accounting in the constrained variant does nothing for both charge and uncharge.
Creation validates flags through a sanitizer before name handling, fails cleanly on sanitizer or allocation errors, and propagates only the close on exec aspect into descriptor installation flags.

Preservation starts with size sampling where empty files yield no folio records. Non empty files estimate folio count from aligned size, pin the full byte range to stabilize pages plus exclude movable memory plus fault in swapped or missing pages, then preserve each folio in order while forcing dirty state plus zeroing and marking up to date any stale folio plus recording physical location with index. The record array itself is preserved as virtual memory with ownership transferred to the caller. Outer preparation freezes the inode plus captures position plus size plus seals after validating seal subset and file size against pin limits, releasing freeze and serialization memory on error. Failures unwind in reverse with unpreserve plus release plus unpin steps.

Freeze refreshes only the saved file position from the live descriptor. Unpreserve reverses preparation by unfreezing plus releasing preserved folio records plus freeing serialization memory. Finish does nothing after successful retrieval and otherwise discards unclaimed restored folios plus frees serialization memory. Discard restores each recorded physical page transiently and drops its reference, warning at a limited rate when restoration fails. Folio unpreserve releases the record array reservation then for each recorded entry releases its folio reservation and unpins it.

Retrieval validates seal compatibility, creates a fresh sealable file, reapplies seals, restores position and size, then rebuilds contents folio by folio. Each entry is restored from its recorded physical location, locked and marked as swap backed, charged to memory control, inserted into the page cache, marked up to date or dirty per saved flags, accounted against inode blocks, added to reclaim and then unlocked with reference dropped. Failures remove the current folio from cache and release later unprocessed entries while retaining already inserted pages for file teardown, always recalculating inode usage.
Preservation eligibility requires a shmem backed file with no directory linkage. Identity for live update matching derives from the backing inode address treated as an unsigned value.

The live update integration exposes an operations table binding freeze plus finish plus retrieve plus preserve plus unpreserve plus eligibility test plus identity fetch plus module ownership, with a handler record pairing that table with a compatibility identity.

Full virtual free forbids non maskable interrupt context, records deallocation for leak tracking, allows sleeping, tolerates null, warns on unknown areas, conditionally resets permissions for areas requiring flush, then releases pages and metadata. The minimal build provides equivalent observable release by delegating directly to heap free.

Alias unmapping serializes with a dedicated mutex while iterating per processor block queues under read side critical sections and per block spin locks. Folio preservation holds each folio lock across dirty and up to date fixup. Live update preparation and cancel hold the inode lock across freeze and serialization steps. Deferred free uses lockless list insertion without additional locking.

Permission reset collects the span of present direct mappings at area page granularity, invalidates direct mappings without flushing, purges aliases over the expanded span, then restores default direct permissions. Direct map updates iterate all pages and affect only those with a direct address, handling huge areas page by page. Page granularity is zero without architectural huge support and otherwise comes from the area descriptor.

Alias purging does nothing before subsystem initialization. Otherwise it attempts to purge fragmented blocks and expands the flush range to cover dirty subranges, resets per block dirty tracking to prevent repeat flushes, frees purged blocks, then either purges lazy areas over the final range or flushes the kernel translation range when any dirty state was observed.

Area page release skips usage accounting when pages were supplied externally, otherwise decrements virtual allocation accounting per page, releases the range in bulk and clears the corresponding slots.

Pinning the full file range materializes missing pages and can waste memory on sparse files while improving later zeroing of stale pages. Forcing dirty state trades reclaimability for correctness when dirtiness changes after preservation. Pinning also avoids movable and scratch memory hazards. Outer preparation rejects oversized files to avoid silent truncation and rejects unknown seals. Inode allocation warns on number exhaustion when wide numbers are disabled.

Calling the blocking free from interrupt context must defer rather than sleep, while non maskable interrupt context is forbidden for both blocking and atomic paths. Freeing an unknown area indicates caller error and warns without further action. Direct mappings are poisoned before translation flush to avoid caching stale entries after unmap.

Observed virtual area state includes flags plus page count plus page array plus optional huge page order. Superblock accounting state includes lock plus quota enable plus free space plus next number plus full width mode plus per processor batch storage plus policy pointer. Folio preservation records carry physical location plus flag bits plus file index. Main preservation records carry position plus size plus seal set plus folio count plus embedded folio array reservation.

Mapping facts are that FS_NOATIME_FL selects S_NOATIME and FS_APPEND_FL selects S_APPEND and FS_IMMUTABLE_FL selects S_IMMUTABLE while FS_NODUMP_FL selects nothing and S_CASEFOLD participates in the mask and FS_CASEFOLD_FL controls the folding bit. Descriptor facts are that MFD_CLOEXEC selects O_CLOEXEC. Failure facts are ENOSPC plus ENOTDIR plus ENOTEMPTY plus EOPNOTSUPP for allocation and flag paths.

Preservation facts are that MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_DIRTY with MEMFD_LUO_FOLIO_UPTODATE mark every saved folio and MEMFD_LUO_ALL_SEALS bounds accepted seals and MEMFD_LUO_FH_COMPATIBLE identifies the handler and MFD_ALLOW_SEALING allows seal restore with MAX_LFS_FILESIZE bounding position. Virtual facts are VM_FLUSH_RESET_PERMS triggering permission reset and VM_MAP_PUT_PAGES skipping accounting with NR_VMALLOC as the accounting tag. Logging facts are fixed prefixes for live update and memory failure with trace creation enabled.
